profile.theme_hint: Light or dark, remembered on this device.

languages.head: Languages
languages.title: Languages
languages.lead: The languages the sign-in pages can be shown in, and — for English and Russian only — this panel. Their text lives in the database: add a language, translate it here or import a file, and it is on the next page anybody opens — nothing is rebuilt.
languages.drawer_description: Its names, where it is offered, and its text.
languages.offer_hint: Show it in the language picker on the sign-in pages.
languages.make_default_hint: What somebody sees before they have chosen. Making this the default takes the mark from whichever language has it.
languages.default_locked: The default language is always offered.
languages.base_note: This is the language every other is a translation of: a key another language has no text for is shown in it. It cannot be turned off or removed.
languages.shipped_note: The server ships a translation of this language, so a key a new release adds is filled in on the next start. Nothing written here is overwritten.
languages.custom_note: Added on this page. A key it has no text for is shown in English until somebody translates it.
languages.name: Name in English
languages.native_hint: What the language picker shows, so people can find their own.
languages.remove_confirm: Its text goes with it, and anybody who chose it gets the default from their next page.
languages.load_failed: Could not load the text. Close this and try again.
languages.imported: {count} texts imported from {file}. Save to keep them.
languages.imported_skipped: {count} keys this version does not use were skipped.
languages.import_invalid: {file} is not a translation file: it has to be one JSON object of texts by key.
languages.placeholder_missing: Keep {names} in the text: it is filled in when the page is shown.
languages.new_description: It starts off, so it can be translated before anybody is offered it.
languages.restore_hint: The server ships these translations, and this installation does not have them.
languages.code_hint: A language tag: uz, de, pt-BR.
languages.code_invalid: A language tag is two or three letters, then optionally a region: de, pt-BR.
languages.code_taken: There is already a language with this code.
languages.start_empty: Nothing — untranslated text is shown in English
languages.offer_now_hint: Otherwise it stays off until you turn it on, so it can be translated first.
languages.panel_only: The admin panel is shown only in English and Russian

error.language_code_taken: There is already a language with this code.
error.language_copy_missing: There is no language {code} to copy.
error.language_default_required: Make another language the default rather than unmarking this one.
error.language_default_protected: Make another language the default before removing this one.
error.language_base_protected: English is what every other language falls back to, so it stays.
error.panel_languages_only: The admin panel is shown only in English and Russian.

sso.head: SSO integrations
sso.title: SSO integrations
sso.lead: Let an organisation sign its people in through its own identity provider — Okta, Microsoft Entra ID, Google Workspace, ADFS — over OpenID Connect or SAML 2.0. A connection owns email domains: the people at them sign in through it, can be made to, and get accounts and roles from what the provider says.
sso.empty_body: Connect a company's identity provider and its people sign in with their work account: routed there by their email domain, given an account the first time, and roles from the groups the provider puts them in.
sso.protocol_oidc_hint: Okta, Entra ID, Google Workspace, Keycloak, Auth0 and most modern providers
sso.protocol_saml_hint: ADFS, Entra ID, Okta, OneLogin, Shibboleth and most enterprise providers
sso.new_description: An organisation's identity provider. It starts off, so it can be set up and tested before anybody signs in through it.
sso.edit_description: Where it signs people in, for which domains, and what they become here.
sso.name: Name
sso.name_hint: What the sign-in page calls it: “Continue with {name}”.
sso.slug_hint: In the addresses the provider is given, so it cannot change. Made from the name unless you give one.
sso.enabled_hint: Off, nobody signs in through it — set it up and test it first.
sso.oidc_description: Register this server at the provider as a web application, then copy its issuer and credentials here.
sso.issuer_hint: Its discovery document is read from the issuer's /.well-known/openid-configuration.
sso.client_secret_stored: A secret is stored. Type a new one to replace it.
sso.scopes_hint: Space separated. openid is always asked for; email and profile unless you name others.
sso.saml_description: Give the provider this server's metadata, then its own here: from an address, or the file it gave you.
sso.metadata_url_hint: Read when you save, and again with Refresh metadata.
sso.metadata_hint: Or paste the file the provider gave you.
sso.sign_requests_hint: For providers that require it. The certificate is in this server's metadata.
sso.test_ok_oidc: Discovery worked: people are sent to {url} to sign in.
sso.test_unsupported_scopes: The provider does not list {scopes} among its scopes, and some providers — Keycloak among them — refuse the whole sign-in over a scope they do not know. Remove it, or add it at the provider first.
sso.test_ok_saml: The metadata is {entity}'s: people are sent to {url} to sign in.
sso.save_first: Create the connection to get the addresses its provider needs.
sso.sp_oidc_description: Register this redirect URI with the application at the provider.
sso.sp_saml_description: Give the provider the metadata URL — or, if it asks for them one by one, these.
sso.idp_expiring: Its certificate expires on {when}. Refresh the metadata once the provider has rolled it over.
sso.domains_hint: People with an address at these domains sign in through this connection, and it signs in nobody else. Leave it empty to trust the provider with any address; people then reach it through its button only.
sso.enforce_hint: Their password sign-in, registration and password reset are refused; the sign-in page sends them to the provider instead.
sso.enforce_needs_domain: Add a domain first: SSO is required of the addresses at its domains.
sso.show_on_login: Show a button on the sign-in page
sso.show_on_login_hint: “Continue with {name}”. Off, people reach it by typing their work address.
sso.matching: An address that already has an account
sso.matching_link: Link it: the provider owns the domain
sso.matching_deny: Refuse: it signs in the way it was made
sso.create_users_hint: Just-in-time provisioning. Off, only people who already have an account here can sign in.
sso.sync_profile_hint: The provider is where they are kept, so a change there reaches here.
sso.attributes_hint: The claim or attribute names. Empty reads the usual ones.
sso.mappings_hint: Everybody the provider puts in a group gets the role, at every sign-in.
sso.no_roles: Your roles do not let you read roles, so you cannot map groups to them.
sso.no_roles_yet: There are no roles yet, so there is nothing to map a group to.
sso.open_roles: Create one on the Roles page
sso.sync_roles_hint: Someone no longer in a group loses its role at their next sign-in. Off, mapped roles are only ever added.
sso.remove_confirm: {count} people sign in through it. They keep their accounts, and sign in however else they can.
sso.need_name: Name the connection to create it.
sso.need_way_in: Add a domain or turn on the sign-in button, on Domains & sign-in, to create it.
sso.need_oidc: Give the issuer and the client ID to create it.
sso.need_metadata: Give the metadata URL or paste the metadata to create it.

sessions.lead: Everyone signed in right now: the browser session that keeps them signed in, where it is and when it started. Sign one out, or sign a user out everywhere — which also revokes the tokens their applications hold, as after a lost device or a compromised account.
sessions.search: Search by the start of an email…
sessions.empty_search: No session belongs to an address starting like that.
sessions.sign_out_user_title: End every session {email} has and revoke their applications' tokens
sessions.confirm_everywhere: Sign {email} out of every browser and every application?
sessions.signed_out: {email} was signed out of {sessions} sessions, and {tokens} application tokens were revoked.

flows.lead: How people sign in, drawn as the steps they go through. Every application follows its own flow, or the default: the password, the other accounts, a verified address and how long a session lasts are all decided here.
flows.template_password_hint: An email and a password, with the accounts from the Social page beside them.
flows.template_passwordless_hint: No passwords here: people sign in with Google, GitHub and the other providers.
flows.template_staff_hint: A password, a verified address, no sign-ups, and eight-hour sessions.
flows.template_blank_hint: An email and a password, and nothing else to start from.
flows.delete_confirm: Delete this flow? {count} applications fall back to the default.
flows.read_only: Your roles let you look at login flows, not change them.
flows.leave_unsaved: This flow has changes that are not saved. Leave anyway?
flows.problem_slug: The identifier has to be lower case letters, numbers and dashes.
flows.problem_proof: Add Password or Other accounts: without one, nobody can sign in.
flows.problem_default_off: The default flow cannot be turned off.
flows.problem_lifetime: A session has to last between one hour and ninety days.
flows.import_not_flow: That file is not a login flow exported from here.
flows.palette_hint: Drag a step onto the flow, or click it to add it at the end.
flows.palette_waiting: Choose the step to add where you clicked +.
flows.section_flow_hint: What the flow is called, here and wherever it is exported.
flows.name: Name
flows.slug_hint: Made from the name unless you change it.
flows.slug_fixed: It names the flow in exports, so it stays as it was made.
flows.enabled_hint: Off, the applications that name it use the default flow instead.
flows.default_hint: Used by every application that names no flow of its own.
flows.default_is: It is the default. Make another flow the default to change that.
flows.used_default: The default: used by every application without its own flow, and named by {count} more.
flows.section_session_hint: How long somebody stays signed in after going through this flow.
flows.planned_body: The sign-in pages do not run this step yet. It can be placed as a plan; the flow still needs Password or Other accounts to let anybody in.
flows.allow_registration_hint: Offers “Create one” on the sign-in page, where the application allows it too.
flows.require_verified_hint: An account whose address is unconfirmed is sent a link instead of being signed in.
flows.identifier_fixed: Every flow starts by asking who is signing in, so this step cannot move or be removed.
flows.allow_reset_hint: A link to reset the password by email. Completing it also confirms the address.
flows.social_hint: Shows a button for each provider turned on at
flows.step_identifier_hint: Ask for the email address the account is under.
flows.step_social_hint: Offer the providers on the Social page: Google, GitHub and the rest.
flows.step_email_code_hint: Send a one-time code to the address and ask for it.
flows.step_totp_hint: Ask for a code from an authenticator app.
flows.step_terms_hint: Ask a new account to accept the terms and privacy policy.
flows.step_consent_hint: Show what the application asks for and wait to be allowed.
